target.title: CAT-Net: A Cross-Attention Tone Network for Cross-Subject EEG-EMG Fusion Tone Decoding
target.venue: AAAI 2026 (first-page copyright identifies AAAI; venue is not otherwise named on the first page)

read.pdf: Tables 1–6, A1, B1, C1–C3 and captions for Figs. 1–3, B1–B6, D1 read in text.txt; graphical figure contents were not available

entries.text: The abstract reports 4,800 EEG trials and 4,800 EMG trials from 10 participants using 20 EEG and 5 EMG channels; it does not distinguish audible from silent trials in this count.
entries.value: 4,800 EEG trials; 4,800 EMG trials; 10 participants; 20 EEG channels; 5 EMG channels
entries.condition: Abstract-level dataset summary; four-tone task; both audible and silent conditions are studied, but the abstract does not specify whether the counts are per condition or pooled.
entries.quote: We collected 4,800 EEG trials and 4,800 EMG trials from 10 participants using only twenty EEG and five EMG channels, demonstrating the feasibility of minimal-channel decoding.

entries.text: The study enrolled ten healthy native Mandarin-speaking adults aged 24–35 years.
entries.condition: Healthy native Mandarin speakers; all participants completed audible and silent articulation conditions.

entries.text: Each of four Mandarin tone categories used 30 characters, each presented four times; the complete set was presented in both articulation modes.
entries.value: 4 tones; 30 characters per tone; 4 repetitions; 480 trials
entries.unit: classes; characters per class; repetitions; trials per complete stimulus set
entries.condition: Pseudorandomized presentation; methods say all 480 trials were completed in both articulation conditions. The abstract's 4,800-per-modality total does not clarify whether that count is per mode or pooled.

entries.text: Signals were acquired with a 64-channel EEG system and EMG from five orofacial muscles at 1000 Hz; the principal experiments use 20 selected EEG channels and five EMG channels.
entries.value: 64 acquired EEG channels; 5 EMG muscles; 1000; 20 EEG channels used in principal experiments
entries.condition: EEG and EMG synchronized; principal experiments are multimodal; EMG sites were right/left buccinator, right/left cervical trapezius, and mentalis.
entries.quote: was recorded using a high-density 64-channel NeuSen W

entries.text: EEG and EMG were downsampled to 500 Hz, bandpass- and 50-Hz notch-filtered, CAR-referenced, epoched from −2 to 2 seconds, and baseline-corrected from −2 to 0 seconds; EEG also underwent ICA artifact removal.
entries.unit: Hz sampling rate; Hz notch frequency; seconds relative to stimulus onset
entries.condition: EEG preprocessing additionally includes ICA to identify/remove ocular and muscular artifacts; EMG preprocessing description does not mention ICA.

entries.text: The preprocessed input sequence has T=500 samples and concatenates each raw channel with its first-order temporal difference, yielding an effective sequence length of 499.
entries.condition: Paired EEG and EMG input; feature dimensions are twice the number of channels for each modality.

entries.text: The authors present CAT-Net as a novel three-stage multimodal EEG–EMG framework with separate spatial-temporal encoders, bidirectional cross-attention, and a fused tone classifier/domain discriminator.
entries.condition: Four Mandarin tone classes; audible and silent speech; domain discriminator is used during training.
entries.quote:
To effectively model the neural-muscular coordination in speech, we propose a model that we call CAT-Net, [C]ross-
[A]ttention [T]one Net, a three-stage architecture designed for multimodal EEG-EMG fusion

entries.text: The stated novelty is cross-attention that lets EEG and EMG attend to each other, replacing simple concatenation/basic fusion to capture bidirectional neural-muscular interactions.
entries.condition: Cross-modal fusion in the four-tone classifier.

entries.text: Training uses a tone focal loss and a subject-label domain discriminator behind a gradient-reversal layer; the paper says this encourages subject-invariant features.
entries.value: γ=2; α=(0.2, 0.3, 0.2, 0.3); λdom=0.05 in the appendix settings
entries.condition: Subject labels identify the ten training subjects; the discriminator is a training head and the tone classifier predicts four classes.
entries.loc: Sec. Domain Discriminator and Loss Functions; Table A1

entries.text: Appendix A reports Adam, learning rate 1e-3, batch size 64, 50 epochs, dropout 0.4, five-fold cross-validation, and early-stopping patience 10 for all experiments.
entries.unit: learning rate; samples per batch; epochs; dropout rate; folds; epochs of patience
entries.condition: Table A1 says settings apply to all experiments; ReduceLROnPlateau factor 0.5, patience 5, minimum learning rate 1e-5; 20 EEG and 5 EMG channels.

entries.text: CAT-Net uses four-head multi-head cross-attention with K=V=32 and directly classifies the fused representation into four Mandarin tones.
entries.condition: One directional attention operation for each modality; global average and max pooling feed a dense layer and tone classifier.

entries.text: The authors claim attention-based channel importance analysis supports effective tone decoding with a minimal 20 EEG plus 5 EMG channels.
entries.condition: Channels selected using EEG channel-attention weights aggregated after training; principal later experiments use the reduced EEG configuration.
entries.quote: We demonstrate effective tone classification using a minimal channel configuration of only 20 EEG channels and 5 EMG channels, selected through attention-based channel importance analysis

entries.text: Table 1 reports mean accuracies and kappa values for EEG-channel-count ablations: 5 channels 86.92%/0.8249; 10 channels 87.02%/0.8251; 20 channels 88.08%/0.8415; full EEG 88.45%/0.8496.
entries.condition: K-fold cross-validation runs; audible/silent mode is not specified in Table 1; 5 EMG channels are used with each EEG-channel configuration.

entries.text: The paper reports 88.08% average accuracy in silent speech and 87.83% in audible speech, using 20 EEG and 5 EMG channels in five-fold cross-validation.
entries.condition: Four-tone classification; ten participants; 20 EEG plus 5 EMG channels; five-fold training/testing. The fold assignment unit is not specified.
entries.quote: As shown in Table 3, our proposed method achieves the highest average accuracy of 88.08% and kappa value of 0.8415 in the silent speech condition.
entries.loc: Sec. Baseline Comparisons, K-Fold Cross Validation; Table 3; Table C3

entries.text: Cohen's kappa is 0.8415 for silent speech and 0.8377 for audible speech; the reported four-class average accuracies are 88.08% and 87.83%, respectively.
entries.condition: Five-fold evaluation on the study data, four tones, 20 EEG and 5 EMG channels; kappa uncertainty or confidence intervals are not reported.
entries.loc: Sec. Baseline Comparisons; Tables 3 and C3

entries.text: For silent speech, Table 3 gives CAT-Net tone precisions of 98.67%, 83.64%, 87.27%, and 83.10%, average 88.08%, and kappa 0.8415.

entries.condition: Silent speech, 20 EEG and 5 EMG channels, four tone classes; five-fold baseline comparison as described in the surrounding section.

entries.condition: Audible speech, 20 EEG and 5 EMG channels, four tone classes; five-fold evaluation described in the main text.

entries.text: In silent speech, CAT-Net's macro F1 and recall are 88.08% and 88.06%; tone-wise F1/recall are T1 99.54/99.83, T2 81.45/80.36, T3 87.91/87.58, and T4 82.54/84.33.
entries.condition: Silent speech, 20 EEG plus 5 EMG channels, four tone classes; five-fold baseline evaluation context.

entries.text: In audible speech, CAT-Net's macro F1 and recall are 87.82% and 87.83%; tone-wise F1/recall are T1 99.50/99.67, T2 81.03/80.08, T3 88.76/89.17, and T4 81.97/82.42.
entries.condition: Audible speech, 20 EEG plus 5 EMG channels, four tone classes; five-fold baseline evaluation context.

entries.text: The authors claim CAT-Net outperforms all listed baselines in both speech conditions and has better performance on difficult Tone 2 and Tone 4 than competing methods.
entries.condition: Main text's five-fold comparison; silent and audible modes; CAT-Net uses EEG and EMG, while baseline input handling is described separately.
entries.loc: Sec. Baseline Comparisons, K-Fold Cross Validation

entries.text: For baselines that do not ordinarily use EMG, the authors state they concatenate EEG and EMG signals as model input.
entries.condition: Applies to baseline comparison; the paper does not provide per-baseline input-shape or implementation details in this statement.
entries.quote:
For algo-
rithms that are not utilizing EMG signals, we concatenate EEG and EMG signals as input to the model.
entries.loc: Sec. Baseline Comparisons, K-Fold Cross Validation

entries.text: In silent-speech LOSO, CAT-Net's mean accuracy is 85.10% across ten held-out subjects; Table 4 reports subject scores S1–S10 as 53.33, 79.58, 82.71, 85.00, 87.08, 91.67, 95.00, 89.17, 94.79, and 92.71%.
entries.condition: Silent speech; leave-one-subject-out, one subject held out and nine remaining subjects for training; 20 EEG and 5 EMG channels; four tones.

entries.text: In audible-speech LOSO, CAT-Net's mean accuracy is 83.27% across ten subjects; Table C2 reports S1–S10 as 56.04, 72.08, 75.42, 80.63, 92.08, 90.00, 91.87, 90.62, 94.79, and 89.17%.
entries.condition: Audible speech; leave-one-subject-out, one subject held out and nine remaining subjects for training; 20 EEG and 5 EMG channels; four tones.
entries.loc: Table C2; Appendix C, Cross Subject Results

entries.text: The authors report a silent-speech accuracy drop of 2.98% from five-fold to LOSO; they report audible-speech results of 87.83% and 83.27% for those protocols without stating the difference.
entries.condition: Silent: 88.08% five-fold to 85.10% LOSO; audible: 87.83% five-fold to 83.27% LOSO; 10 subjects.

entries.text: The authors describe CAT-Net as more robust on abnormal unseen subjects and say it beats the second-best baseline on S1, S3, and S4 by 6.8, 6.25, and 2.5 percentage points, respectively, in the reported cross-subject analysis.
entries.unit: authors report as % higher than second-best baseline; denominator interpretation not specified
entries.condition: Cross-subject comparison; the paper does not define the operational criterion for 'abnormal' subjects.

entries.text: Appendix C claims CAT-Net achieves the highest accuracy on all ten subjects, but its displayed audio LOSO table has CAT-Net below GAT on S10 and tied with EEGNet on S9; Table 4 also has silent CAT-Net below DeepConvNet on S9.
entries.condition: Comparison is read directly from the paper's own Table 4 and Table C2 subject-level LOSO values.
entries.quote:
Moreover, CATNet demonstrates remarkable stability and consistency, achieving the highest accuracy on all 10 sub-
jects.
entries.loc: Appendix C, Cross Subject Results; Tables 4 and C2

entries.text: Cross-subject ablation changes silent-speech mean accuracy from 84.69% without the domain discriminator to 85.10% with it; for S1, accuracy changes from 48.96% to 53.33%.
entries.value: mean 84.69 without DD vs 85.10 with DD; S1 48.96 vs 53.33
entries.condition: Silent speech LOSO; ten subjects; 20 EEG and 5 EMG channels; domain discriminator (DD) ablated.

entries.text: The five-fold ablation reports precision/recall/F1: full CAT-Net 88.08/88.08/88.06%; without cross-attention 77.63/77.62/77.00%; without BiLSTM 78.42/78.42/78.41%; without EMG-to-EEG fusion 76.60/76.60/76.50%; without EEG-to-EMG fusion 76.46/76.46/76.35%.
entries.condition: Five-fold training scenario; Table 6 does not explicitly name the speech condition (the surrounding main-text comparison focuses on silent speech); cross-attention (CT), temporal feature/BiLSTM, feature fusion, and domain discriminator ablations.

entries.text: The authors interpret the ablation as evidence that cross-attention is indispensable for capturing inter-modal dependencies and improving recognition accuracy.
entries.condition: Based on Table 6 five-fold ablation; removal of the full attention module lowers precision from 88.08% to 77.63%.
entries.quote:
These re-
sults confirm that cross-attention is indispensable

entries.text: The authors qualify the domain-discriminator benefit as slight on average in their relatively balanced, minimal-channel dataset and suggest greater benefit in more heterogeneous or low-resource conditions.
entries.condition: Silent cross-subject setting; Table 5 domain-discriminator ablation.
entries.quote: absence of DD leads to a slight drop in average accuracy (from 85.10% to 84.69%)

entries.text: The authors say the 20-channel selection balances discarding less informative electrodes with accuracy; Table 1 reports 88.08% with 20 channels and 88.45% with the full EEG configuration.
entries.condition: Table 1 K-fold cross-validation; silent/audible condition is not stated in the table.
entries.quote: Thus, subsequent experiments will primarily focus on models utilizing a reduced set of 20 EEG channels in the frontal, central, and parietal brain regions.

entries.text: SHAP analysis is interpreted as showing generally greater EMG contribution than EEG for Tones 1, 3, and 4, with greater EEG contribution for Tone 2 under silent speech.

entries.text: The conclusion frames broader modalities/tasks, validation on more diverse datasets, scalability, and real-world deployment as future work rather than established results.
entries.condition: Current evaluation is an offline tone-classification study with ten healthy native Mandarin speakers.

entries.text: ALIGN adversarially trains a domain classifier on encoder latent features and applies the invariance loss at intermediate Transformer layers, using gradient reversal to make representations session-invariant.

entries.text: The adversarial identity is recording session, not subject or speaker: a binary head for each source session distinguishes that session from the pooled target sessions.
entries.condition: Session-level domain labels; no speaker- or subject-classification objective reported.

questions.q: What are the headline results, and under which conditions were they measured?
questions.answer: Five-fold results are 88.08% accuracy (κ=0.8415) for silent speech and 87.83% (κ=0.8377) for audible speech with 20 EEG and 5 EMG channels. LOSO means are 85.10% silent and 83.27% audible across ten held-out subjects.

questions.q: Does the reported five-fold result establish speaker-independent performance?
questions.answer: No speaker-grouped split is specified for five-fold CV, so speaker overlap cannot be determined. The separately reported LOSO evaluation explicitly holds out one subject and trains on the other nine.

questions.q: What reproducibility and selection conditions are missing?
questions.answer: Seeds/repeated runs, fold grouping, validation/checkpoint selection data, fold-wise channel-selection scope, input normalization scope, and vocabulary/repetition split details are not reported.

questions.q: What limitations or unverified deployment claims should a review preserve?
questions.answer: The authors call the domain-discriminator gain slight on average and reserve broader-dataset validation, scalability, and real-world deployment for future work; no online latency or user-facing study is reported.

questions.q: Was public code inspected for conditions omitted from the paper?
questions.answer: The paper links a GitHub repository, but no README or training/evaluation scripts were retrievable, so no code-only conditions are recorded.
